newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Quinn makes provision for budgetary contingencies.
newsitem.headline: Quinn makes provision for budgetary contingencies.

text.p: Irish finance minister Ruairi Quinn said on Wednesday that he had made a net provision against all budgetary contingenices of 175 million punts in 1998 and 325 million in 1999.
This would increase Ireland's projected general government deficit to 1.5 percent of GDP in both 1998 and 1999, he said in his 1997 budget speech.

"Recent experience shows that we should budget for the unexpected. I think it is prudent when making plans over several years to provide a reserve against factors outside the control of the government that may impact on the budget but which cannot be foreseen at this stage," Quinn said.
Variability in tax buoyancy and exceptional costs across all areas of public expenditure were such examples, he said.
"While such variations are likely to be both positive and negative, it is appropriate to allow in the projections for a modest negative net impact on the EBR and GGD," Quinn said.
Before allowing for the budgetary provision, the government had estimated the underlying general government deficit would be 1.2 percent of GDP in 1998 and 0.9 percent in 1999.
